request.text: What is the current on AM1?

solution.item: Solution by TINA assisted by AI
We have more than one generator so we are using superposition to calculate voltages/currents.
>> Pass1 started ...
>> Gen processing: VS1 ...
First we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (VS1)
The total resistance is R1 = 1kOhm
Now we calculate the current on R1
We know that the voltage between VS1 nodes is 0 Volt.
All voltage generators except for VS1 have been replaced with a short circuit.
All current generators have been replaced with an open circuit.
The current on R1 is the voltage on R1/R1 = 0 Amper
>> Pass2 started ...
>> Gen processing: IS1 ...
First we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (IS1)
Ra1=R1=1kOhm=1kOhm
The total resistance is Ra1 = 1kOhm
Now we calculate the current on R1

We know that the voltage between IS1 nodes is 10 Volt, because the generator current is Igen = 10mA and the resistance between the generator nodes is Rtot = 1kOhm so the voltage between the generator nodes is Igen*Rtot = 10 Volt
All voltage generators have been replaced with a short circuit.
All current generators except for IS1 have been replaced with an open circuit.
The components R1 and Rb1 connected in parallel. The voltage on R1 is 10 Volt because the voltage on Ra1 is 10 Volt
The current on R1 is the voltage on R1/R1 = 10m Amper
Now we are using superposition to calculate the current on R1
Let's summarize the calculations from the previous section.
When you see subtraction here it means that the original direction reversed.
'current on R1' = 0A+10mA = 10mA
To answer the original question: because the AM1 ampermeter connected to R1 in series so the current on AM1 is 10m Amper
